rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-4, Tables 3-5 - the authors train and evaluate their own modified MobileNetV2 (SE blocks, residual skip connections) on the PlantVillage dataset (Mohanty et al., 2016), reporting accuracy 0.98 and F1 0.98, plus an ablation study and tests on random online images.
rows.notes: The study reports a leaf-image classification model trained on the public PlantVillage dataset of close-up RGB leaf photographs (38 classes, Table 1); it is not remote sensing or UAV imagery. It classifies images into disease/healthy classes (including late blight and rust classes) but does not grade infection severity, does not show detection before canopy-wide symptoms (images are of symptomatic single leaves), and does not test any targeted response or disease control. Detection is only a precondition of the claimed pest-control effect, and the imaging technology differs from the remote sensing named in the claim. The text's claim of performance under 'real-world field conditions' rests on a qualitative test with random online images (Figure 6), not field remote sensing. Limitations stated (data imbalance, interpretability) and per-class metrics relate to classification, not to the claimed effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. Minor internal inconsistency: abstract and discussion report 98% accuracy while the conclusion states 96%.
